I am 69 years old, my back is not what it used to be, and I never went to school — I cannot read a single word. But I have farmed this land in Quzhou for over fifty years, and I know what works. I will stick to the wheat-maize double-cropping system on my 8 mu of land. Winter wheat is already in the ground from last October, and after we harvest it in early June, I will plant summer maize right away. I do not grow cotton anymore — at my age, bending down to pick it and spraying pesticides fourteen times is too much for these old bones. Vegetables are too risky; prices go up and down, and I do not have the energy to learn new tricks. Wheat and maize are safe: the government gives a subsidy for wheat, the dealers always buy them, and I can hire a combine harvester so I do not have to cut everything by hand. For the wheat, I will topdress with urea when it greens up in spring — about 45 jin of nitrogen per mu — and irrigate three times. I will spray herbicide once, insecticide twice, and fungicide once to keep the diseases away. I rotary-tilled the land before sowing the wheat, and I expect around 1,000 jin per mu. For the maize, I will use Denghai 605, the hybrid seed everyone trusts, and I will plant it no-till straight into the wheat stubble to save labor and diesel. I will put down compound fertilizer at planting, giving about 30 jin of nitrogen per mu, irrigate twice, and spray three times total. I expect about 1,050 jin per mu of maize. This is the same as I have done for decades, and it feeds my family.
